messages:
Kevin: Heads-up — ded-rt-02 showed steady GPU heap creep during long-running chat inference (seq=2048, batch=16). Memory climbs ~20MB/hr until we hit OOM. I added a tiny repro in tools/repro; can someone take a look?

Kevin: repro command I used:
```
python tools/repro/gpu_heap_creep.py --model redwood-small --batch 16 --seq 2048 --iters 500 
# runtime env: RW_PROFILE=1 RW_WORKSPACE_MAX=1024MB
```

Maria: ran the repro with --no-kv-cache; growth still happens but ~3x slower. nvprof/NSYS shows lots of small cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn during token generation.

Maria: nvprof summary snippet:
```
cudaMalloc         1280 calls   avg 9.2KB  total ~11.6MB
cudaFree           1280 calls
cudaMemcpyAsync    many small copies from ephemeral buffers
```

Sophie: hmm this smells like allocator fragmentation from many transient buffers, maybe exacerbated by kernel fallback path (we create temporary workspaces for fallback kernels). When I forced RW_FORCE_KERNEL=prefer_fast the growth stopped on my local VM.

Sophie: try this env + run:
```bash
export RW_FORCE_KERNEL=prefer_fast
export RW_WORKSPACE_MAX=1024MB
python tools/repro/gpu_heap_creep.py --model redwood-small --batch 16 --seq 2048 --iters 500
```

Dave: FWIW I reproduced on a different node and trimming the workspace helps: RW_WORKSPACE_MAX=512MB flattened growth. That points to workspace slabs not KV cache leaking.

Dave: quick log line from my run:
```
[allocator] slab_alloc size=131072 retained=8 slab_frag=0.12 total_reserved=512MB
[token-gen] kernel fallback triggered for head fusion, allocated temp=16KB x 1200
```

PerfBot: NSYS profile uploaded: s3://perf/artifacts/1759001234_nsys.qdrep, flamegraph: s3://perf/artifacts/1759001234_flame.html

Kevin: Good debugging so far. Proposed next steps:
  1) Add transient allocator telemetry: histogram of alloc/free sizes and slab reuse hits/misses.
  2) Exercise no-fallback vs fallback kernel paths at scale and capture NSYS.
  3) Try enabling buffer-reuse path (RW_ALLOC_REUSE=1) to see if it eliminates churn.
  4) If fragmentation persists, add a periodic compact/trim for unused slabs after X idle seconds.

Kevin: I'll open an issue with repro + NSYS + my run logs and assign to Sophie for the root-cause A/B.

Sophie: :thumbsup: I'll run A/B tests tomorrow (no-fallback, workspace caps, alloc_reuse) and post a short table. If alloc_reuse fixes it we can ship the opt behind a flag while we work on a more robust slab compaction.

Maria: also adding a quick quick-check: run with cudaMallocAsync disabled (ENV CUDA_ASYNC_ALLOC=0) — that changed behavior in one of our perf experiments last quarter.

Kevin: thanks all — filing now and linking here once issue exists.
